newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Legal questions around the planned BA/AMR deal.
newsitem.headline: Legal questions around the planned BA/AMR deal.

text.p: The European Commission relaunched on Tuesday its offensive against the proposed alliance between British Airways and AMR's American Airlines, reopening a debate on where legal powers lie.

European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert met British Trade and Industry Secretary Margaret Beckett in London to inform her of what the Commission had already made crystal clear, that the deal will not get the EU blessing as it stands.
The following is a run-down of the key events and legal questions raised by the EU executive's involvement in the BA/American story.

-- July 3, 1996. The Commission launches a probe into six transatlantic airline alliances, including BA/American. It cites Regulation 3975/87 as the legal basis for it to apply EC treaty articles 85 and 86 to the deals, albeit only for services between airports of the European Community. For transatlantic routes, the Commission says treaty article 89 gives it the power to vet each deal in its entirety, in cooperation with national authorities.

-- July 23, 1996. The then British trade Minister Ian Lang announces that Britain's Office of Fair Trading (OFT) will examine the planned BA/American alliance under EC Treaty article 88, in parallel with its ongoing probe under British competition rules. The Commission sees no problem with this.

-- December 6, 1996. After repeated delays, Lang announces that the planned deal will be referred to Britain's Monopolies and Mergers Commission unless the airlines meet certain conditions, adding that even then, approval will hinge on the successful conclusion of a UK/U.S. open skies agreement.

-- January, 1997. Brussels and London engage in a public row through the month over approval conditions for the alliance and who has jurisdiction, a question many lawyers say could be resolved only in the unlikely event of a legal battle in the European Court of Justice.
-- March 24, 1997. Britain's Department of Trade and Industry says it does not expect to make any decisions on BA/American until after Britain's May 1 national election.
-- May 20, 1997. Van Miert meets Beckett in London. A Commission source says companies will be informed of Commission thinking in the coming days and that a statement may be expected by May 23.

-- The Commission is not following a fixed timetable, in contrast to how it operates in most merger inquiries. Article 89 of the Treaty does not specify procedural rules or a timetable under which the Commission must act, meaning action must be under Regulation 3975/87 which talks of acting "without undue delay".
